---
title: getTransactions
description: Returns list of transactions
---

{/* rpc-method: generated from the OpenRPC spec */}

The `getTransactions` method return a detailed list of transactions starting from the user specified starting point that you can paginate as long as the pages fall within the history retention of their corresponding RPC provider.

## Params (3)

<Tip>
Please note that parameter structure within the request must contain named parameters as a by-name object, and not as positional arguments in a by-position array
</Tip>

<ParamField body="startLedger" type="number">
  Ledger sequence number to start fetching responses from (inclusive). This method will return an error if `startLedger` is less than the oldest ledger stored in this node, or greater than the latest ledger seen by this node. If a cursor is included in the request, `startLedger` must be omitted.
  
  Sequence number of the ledger.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="pagination" type="object">
  Pagination in stellar-rpc is similar to pagination in Horizon. See [Pagination](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/data/rpc/api-reference/structure/pagination).
  <Expandable title="properties">
    <ParamField body="cursor" type="string">
      An opaque string which acts as a paging token. To obtain the next page of results occurring after a given response set this value to the `cursor` field of the response.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="limit" type="number">
      The maximum number of records returned. The limit for getTransactions can range from 1 to 200 - an upper limit that is hardcoded in Stellar-RPC for performance reasons. If this argument isn't designated, it defaults to 50.
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="xdrFormat" type="string">
  Lets the user choose the format in which the response should be returned - either as unpacked JSON or as base64-encoded XDR strings. Note that you should not rely on any schema for the JSON, as it will change when the underlying XDR changes.
  
  Specifies whether XDR should be encoded as Base64 (default or 'base64') or JSON ('json').
</ParamField>

## Result

*(getTransactionsResult)*

<ResponseField name="transactions" type="object[]">
  <Expandable title="items">
    <ResponseField name="status" type="string">
      Indicates whether the transaction was successful or not.
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="txHash" type="string">
      The hex-encoded hash of the transaction.
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="applicationOrder" type="number">
      The 1-based index of the transaction among all transactions included in the ledger.
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="feeBump" type="boolean">
      Indicates whether the transaction was fee bumped.
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="envelopeXdr" type="string">
      The [TransactionEnvelope](https://github.com/stellar/stellar-xdr/blob/v22.0/Stellar-transaction.x#L1009) structure for this transaction (base64-encoded string).
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="resultXdr" type="string">
      The [TransactionResult](https://github.com/stellar/stellar-xdr/blob/v22.0/Stellar-transaction.x#L2088) structure for this transaction (base64-encoded string).
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="resultMetaXdr" type="string">
      The [TransactionResultMeta](L446https://github.com/stellar/stellar-xdr/blob/v22.0/Stellar-ledger.x#L461) structure for this transaction (base64-encoded string).
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="diagnosticEventsXdr" type="string[]">
      (optional) A base64 encoded slice of xdr.DiagnosticEvent. This is only present if the `ENABLE_SOROBAN_DIAGNOSTIC_EVENTS` has been enabled on the RPC server.
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="events" type="object">
      Contains all events emitted during transaction execution.
      
      _Note: Available only on RPC v23.x (currently testnet only)._
      <Expandable title="properties">
        <ResponseField name="transactionEventsXdr" type="string[]">
          An array of base64-encoded [xdr.TransactionEvent](https://github.com/stellar/stellar-xdr/blob/v23.0/Stellar-ledger.x#L503-L506). These include events such as fees being charged or refunded.
        </ResponseField>
        <ResponseField name="contractEventsXdr" type="string[][]">
          A nested array of base64-encoded [xdr.ContractEvent](https://github.com/stellar/stellar-xdr/blob/v23.0/Stellar-ledger.x#L371-L390). Each inner array represents the contract events emitted by a single operation within the transaction.
        </ResponseField>
      </Expandable>
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="ledger" type="number">
      The sequence number of the ledger which included the transaction.
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="createdAt" type="number">
      The unix timestamp of when the transaction was included in the ledger.
    </ResponseField>
  </Expandable>
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="latestLedger" type="number">
  The sequence number of the latest ledger known to Stellar RPC at the time it handled the request.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="latestLedgerCloseTimestamp" type="number">
  The unix timestamp of the close time of the latest ledger known to Stellar RPC at the time it handled the request.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="oldestLedger" type="number">
  The sequence number of the oldest ledger ingested by Stellar RPC at the time it handled the request.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="oldestLedgerCloseTimestamp" type="number">
  The unix timestamp of the close time of the oldest ledger ingested by Stellar RPC at the time it handled the request.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="cursor" type="string">
  A token which can be included in a subsequent request to obtain the next page of results.
</ResponseField>

## Examples

<Tabs>
<Tab title="Successful getTransactions Request">

Query a list of transactions starting from the given startLedger.

**Request**

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
curl -X POST \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d '{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 8675309,
  "method": "getTransactions",
  "params": {
    "startLedger": 337272,
    "pagination": {
      "limit": 5
    }
  }
}' \
https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org | jq
```

```js JavaScript
let requestBody = {
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 8675309,
  "method": "getTransactions",
  "params": {
    "startLedger": 337272,
    "pagination": {
      "limit": 5
    }
  }
}
let res = await fetch('https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
  },
  body: JSON.stringify(requestBody),
})
let json = await res.json()
console.log(json)
```

```python Python
import json, requests
res = requests.post("https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org", json={
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": 8675309,
    "method": "getTransactions",
    "params": {
        "startLedger": 337272,
        "pagination": {
            "limit": 5
        }
    }
})
print(json.dumps(res.json(), indent=4))
```

<Tab title="Successful getTransactions Request Using Cursor">

Query a list of transactions starting from the given cursor.

**Request**

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
curl -X POST \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d '{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 8675309,
  "method": "getTransactions",
  "params": {
    "pagination": {
      "cursor": "1448572209676993",
      "limit": 5
    }
  }
}' \
https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org | jq
```

### Using the Lab

The `getTransactions` method returns a **paginated list of transactions** starting from a user-defined point. You can continue paginating through results as long as the requested range falls within the **history retention window** of the corresponding RPC provider.

Use this method in the [Stellar Laboratory](https://laboratory.stellar.org) to explore recent activity within a given time frame or ledger range.

👉 [View Transactions on the Lab](https://lab.stellar.org/endpoints/rpc/get-transactions?$=network$id=testnet&label=Testnet&horizonUrl=https:////horizon-testnet.stellar.org&rpcUrl=https:////soroban-testnet.stellar.org&passphrase=Test%20SDF%20Network%20/;%20September%202015;&endpoints$params$startLedger=573331;;)
